summary: ```# Marvelous Designer 12 New Feature Demonstration: Merge Vertices Based on Proximity ## Introduction In this demonstration, we will explore the new feature in Marvelous Designer 12 that allows users to merge vertices based on proximity. This feature enhances the design process by allowing more precise adjustments and seamless integration of garment panels. ## Setting Up the Transparent Pot According to the proximity of the joint points, start by opening the clothing of a transparent pot. 1. Select the **Transparent Pot Tool** in either the 2D or 3D window. 2. You will see the blue transparent pot grid displayed in the window. ## Adjusting the Transparent Pot Position In the video, we deliberately created the wrong transparent pot position. - Right-click to reopen the menu. - Click "All" to reset the grid. The newly created panels will automatically be generated on top of the original panel while maintaining the original panel shape. ## Selecting Panel Outlines Next, select all panel outlines in the display settings of the 2D window: 1. Click and drag the mouse to select the panels to reset the grid. 2. Move them to a position where they do not overlap with the original panel. ## Locking and Unlocking Panels If you want to reverse the lock: - Go to the display settings and unlock all panel outlines. - After resetting, click to lock all panels. At this stage, you can only select the panels that were originally created in the 3D window. Move them to the panels that do not overlap with the original panel. ## Saving the OBJ File To save your work: 1. Find the folder window and click "Undo." 2. Click "OBJ," then enter the folder name and click "Save." When the OBJ is exported and opened, select the points that are close to each other. ## Merging Vertices When selecting this option, a 3D window will appear at the bottom: - The top of the merge will be shown in red, while the top that cannot be merged will be shown in blue. Now, let's take a look at the grid part that was left empty before. Adjust the merge distance to a larger or smaller value. The larger the gap, the greater the merge distance. Once the effect is satisfactory, click on the bottom of the OBJ window to confirm that the grid will be merged. ## Viewing in Other 3D Software Open the OBJ file in other 3D software. You will see that, although there is no merge line, the top points of the edge of the panel are still combined. The merge close to the top point function will also work on panels that have a merge line relationship and panels that do not have a merge line relationship. ## Conclusion The merge function accounts for both the bezier and the transverse triangle on Projeto5. Now, let's perform the Wolf II modification: - Here, the merge does not create a merge line. - This method is soon complete from scratch, enhancing the design process significantly. By utilizing these new features in Marvelous Designer 12, designers can achieve greater efficiency and precision in their garment construction. ```
